subject: Request: AWS Marketplace commission exception & SLA alignment for CloudCorp Enterprise
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Santos <alice.santos@cloudcorp.com>, Mark Zhou <mark.zhou@amazon.com>
Cc: CloudCorp Procurement <procurement@cloudcorp.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Initial: CloudCorp Enterprise — pricing / rev-share question

Hi Alice / Mark,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. CloudCorp is ready to move forward with a private offer via the AWS Marketplace. Before we generate the private offer, procurement has two asks that need approval from our side: a 40% rev-share carveout for a co-sell credit structure (CloudCorp is requesting 40% for the first 12 months) and a tighter SLA (99.9% uptime with an uptime rebate mechanism). Those terms sit outside of our standard marketplace playbook.

Attached is a draft of the private offer bundle and the SOW. Can you confirm whether AWS can accept a 40% rev-share for year one and whether Redwood can commit to the proposed SLA language (we would need legal sign-off on the rebate clause)? If AWS requires a different revenue split in the marketplace record, call that out and we can escalate to deal desk.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Mark/Marketplaces: confirm whether a 40% rev-share is feasible on the AWS private-offer flow or whether Marketplace policies force us to cap at 30%.
- Legal/Revenue: if 40% cannot be supported directly, provide an approved alternative (commission carve-out or one-time credit).
- Redwood: if SLA language requires an exception, route for exec approval.

I will loop in our Deal Desk for anything that needs an exception.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0134

Attachments: CloudCorp_SOW_v3.pdf; AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft.json; pricing_spreadsheet.xlsx
From: Alice Santos <alice.santos@cloudcorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudCorp Procurement <procurement@cloudcorp.com>, Mark Zhou <mark.zhou@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: CloudCorp Enterprise — pricing / rev-share question

Jonas — thanks for the materials. A few clarifications from procurement:

1) The 40% rev-share is a hard requirement for our sales team for the first 12 months. We are open to a stepped-down rate in year two, but year one must be 40% to meet our compensation plan.
2) SLA: the rebate language is standard for us — we need a credit of 10% of monthly invoice for downtime exceeding 0.1%. Can Redwood accept that, or will an operational play (multi-region failover) suffice?
3) Timing: we need a binding private offer by Oct 8 to align with our quarter close.

Mark — can AWS confirm whether the private-offer flow allows a 40% split as a carveout, or whether the offer metadata will block that? If not, we need to understand the marketplace-compliant workaround (e.g., seller-side credit, promo code).

Thanks,
Alice Santos
Director, Cloud Procurement — CloudCorp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Santos <alice.santos@cloudcorp.com>, Mark Zhou <mark.zhou@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: CloudCorp Enterprise — pricing / rev-share question (need exec exception)

Laura / Karthik / Marissa — forwarding the ask from CloudCorp: they require a 40% rev-share for year one and an SLA rebate (10% monthly credit if downtime > 0.1%). AWS/Mark, please chime in on marketplace constraints.

Why this is an exception: our current marketplace guidance caps standard rev-share at 30% for promotional carveouts; anything above requires Deal Desk + Finance approval. SLA rebate with financial liability is also outside of our standard private-offer obligations and would require Legal + Finance signoff and an exec commit.

Key constraints and impact:
- Revenue math: a 40% split cuts our net by ~10 percentage points vs. a 30% baseline for year one (see attached pricing_spreadsheet.xlsx).
- Compensation: CloudCorp will attribute full ACV to their reps if we agree — meaningful ARR acceleration but lower unit economics for Redwood in year one.
- Precedent risk: approving 40% sets a precedent for enterprise marketplace co-sell deals.

Suggested options for quick decision (we need to reply to CloudCorp by EOD Oct 2 to make the Oct 8 private offer):
A) Approve 40% for yr1 as a one-off; require a buy-down to 25% in year 2; require a one-time onboarding credit to Redwood sales to offset comp leakage.
B) Cap marketplace rev-share at 30% and provide CloudCorp a seller-side credit equal to the delta (handled as a separate redemption off-invoice for first 12 months).
C) Decline 40% and propose a 30% rev-share plus a contractual performance rebate tied to uptime (but limit liability to a not-to-exceed cap).

Please advise ASAP on which option to approve so I can respond to Alice. If option A is selected, we need LAURA or a named exec to sign off (revenue tolerance + precedent).

Jonas
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Santos <alice.santos@cloudcorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudCorp Enterprise — pricing / rev-share question (need exec exception)

Jonas — appreciate the clear options. I spoke with Finance and CS leads. My recommendation: we approve Option B (cap at 30% on the marketplace record and issue a seller-side monthly credit to CloudCorp equal to the 10% delta for year one). Rationale: preserves marketplace constraints, avoids changing marketplace precedent, and gives CloudCorp the economic they need while keeping the contract and revenue recognition clean for Redwood.

Conditions that must be documented before we sign:
- Seller-side credit will be paid monthly as a contra-revenue credit and capped at the ACV listed in the pricing_spreadsheet.xlsx.
- SLA rebate language: accept the 10% monthly credit trigger but limit Redwood's exposure to a maximum of 2 months of credits in any 12-month period (operational cap).
- Legal to approve precise language and ensure the credit is handled as contra-revenue (Marissa, please prepare redline to SOW and private-offer notes).
- Deal Desk to log a one-off commission carve-out for CloudCorp sales (comp plan impact to be handled by RevOps).

If Finance confirms the contra-revenue handling, I will sign off on the one-off seller-side credit. We still need an AWS confirmation that the private-offer metadata can surface a 30% marketplace rev-share and allow external seller credits. Mark — can you confirm?

Laura Bennett
VP, Head of Revenue | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Santos <alice.santos@cloudcorp.com>, Mark Zhou <mark.zhou@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudCorp Enterprise — pricing / rev-share question (need exec exception)

All — legal + Deal Desk have reviewed and we can proceed on Laura's conditional path (Option B) with the following deliverables:

1) I attached a redlined SOW and an amendment that documents the seller-side monthly contra-credit and the SLA cap. Once CloudCorp signs, our finance team will book the credit as contra-revenue.
2) AWS confirmation: Mark, please confirm that the private-offer can be published with 30% marketplace rev-share and that the external seller credit can be processed off-invoice (we will not populate a 40% split in the marketplace metadata). If AWS requires a promo-code or separate redemption mechanism, include steps in your reply.
3) Execution steps for Jonas:
   - Update the AWS private-offer draft to 30% in the public metadata and attach the seller-credit amendment as a non-marketplace contractual addendum.
   - Send the revised docs to CloudCorp for signature and route DocuSign to laura.bennett for final sign-off.

DocuSign link for the amendment: https://docusign.com/s/rdw/exec/cc-834 (placeholder)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/834

We will hold precedent by documenting this as a one-off, flagged in Deal Desk. Jonas — please proceed with the revision and let me know when you have the signed amendment; finance will prepare the contra-revenue schedule.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: CloudCorp_SOW_v3_Redline.pdf
